facts.statement: Utahraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically from the Berriasian to the Valanginian stages, with a possible record extending into the Hauterivian–Barremian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Berriasian – Valanginian), Possible Hauterivian–Barremian record

facts.statement: The genus Utahraptor was described by James Kirkland, Robert Gaston, and Donald Burge in 1993.
facts.quote: authority: Kirkland, Gaston & Burge, 1993

facts.statement: The type species Utahraptor ostrommaysi was named in 1993 based on fossils found in the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah.
facts.quote: The genus was described in 1993 by American paleontologist James Kirkland and colleagues with the type species Utahraptor ostrommaysi, based on fossils that had been unearthed earlier from the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah.

facts.statement: Utahraptor is the largest known member of the family Dromaeosauridae, measuring approximately 6 to 7 meters in length and weighing around 500 kilograms.
facts.quote: It is the largest-known member of the family Dromaeosauridae, measuring about 6 - 7 m long and typically weighing around 500 kg.

facts.statement: Utahraptor hunted ankylosaurs and iguanodonts in the Cedar Mountain Formation ecosystem.
facts.quote: Being a carnivore, Utahraptor was adapted to hunt the other animals of the Cedar Mountain Formation ecosystem such as ankylosaurs and iguanodonts.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Utahraptor was an ambush predator, unlike other dromaeosaurs which were pursuit predators.
facts.quote: Evidence from the leg physiology supports the idea of Utahraptor being an ambush predator, in contrast to other dromaeosaurs that were pursuit predators.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Utahraptor was social and practiced some form of post-nestling care.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of several individuals of various ages have been found together, suggesting that Utahraptor was gregarious (social) and practiced degrees of post nestling care.

facts.statement: The first Utahraptor specimens were discovered in 1975 by Jim Jensen in the Dalton Wells Quarry near Moab, Utah.
facts.quote: The first specimens of Utahraptor were found in 1975 by Jim Jensen in the Dalton Wells Quarry of Utah, near the town of Moab, but did not receive much attention.

facts.statement: Further Utahraptor remains were uncovered in 1991 by James Kirkland, Robert Gaston, and Donald Burge in the Gaston Quarry, Grand County, Utah.
facts.quote: After the find of a large claw by Carl Limone in October 1991, James Kirkland, Robert Gaston and Donald Burge uncovered further remains of Utahraptor in 1991 in the Gaston Quarry in Grand County, Utah, within the Yellow Cat and Poison Strip members of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

facts.statement: The type species Utahraptor ostrommaysi was named in June 1993 by Kirkland, Gaston, and Burge.
facts.quote: The type species, Utahraptor ostrommaysi, was named by Kirkland, Gaston and Burge in June 1993.

facts.statement: The genus name Utahraptor refers to Utah, the location where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The genus name Utahraptor is in reference to Utah, where the remains were found.

facts.statement: The specific name ostrommaysi honors John Ostrom and Chris Mays for their contributions to the research of Utahraptor.
facts.quote: The specific name, ostrommaysi, is in honor to John Ostrom for his investigations on Deinonychus and its relationships to birds, as well as Chris Mays, who helped in the research of Utahraptor by founding Dinamation.

facts.statement: The name was changed from U. spielbergi to U. ostrommaysi shortly before publication due to pressure from Universal Studios regarding the use of "Jurassic" in museum exhibits.
facts.quote: Kirkland, however, later expressed that this was a misquote. He had changed the name to U. ostrommaysi shortly before the publication of the paper, as Universal Studios has begun threatening to sue museums that have exhibits with the word "Jurassic" in their titles; Dinamation, Kirkland's employers with connections to various museums, thus implored him to change the name, which he did.

facts.statement: In 2000, George Olshevsky emended the specific name to ostrommaysorum.
facts.quote: In 2000, the specific name was emended by George Olshevsky to the plural genitive ostrommaysorum.

facts.statement: In 2019, Costa and David criticized the emended name ostrommaysorum, arguing it lacks clear justification.
facts.quote: However, Thiago Vernaschi V. Costa and Normand David in 2019 criticized the use of the species name U. ostrommaysorum, since it has no clear justification or explanation.

facts.statement: A lacrimal bone previously assigned to Utahraptor was later identified as a postorbital bone from the ankylosaur Gastonia.
facts.quote: Some elements were wrongly referred to the genus. The lacrimal bone of the specimen CEUM 184v.83 turned out to be a postorbital from the ankylosaur Gastonia.

facts.statement: Utahraptor was one of the largest dromaeosaurids, with some of its largest bones being slightly larger than those of Achillobator.
facts.quote: Utahraptor was one of the largest dromaeosaurids, with the largest elements assigned to the genus being slightly larger than the same bones in Achillobator.

facts.statement: Based on evidence of filamentation in related dromaeosaurs, Utahraptor ostrommaysi was likely feathered.
facts.quote: Based on evidence of filamentation in other dromaeosaurs, U. ostrommaysi was likely feathered.

facts.statement: In 2024, higher mass estimates were recovered, with some specimens estimated to weigh up to 777 kg.
facts.quote: In 2024, higher mass estimates were once again recovered by Romain Pintore and colleagues. The body masses of BYUVP 2536 and BYUVP 1833 were estimated around 391 and 481 kg, respectively, while BYUVP 7510-18078 was estimated to have weighed 777 kg.

facts.statement: Utahraptor is classified as a large dromaeosaurid dinosaur, a group of feathered carnivorous theropods.
facts.quote: Utahraptor (meaning "Utah's predator") is a genus of large dromaeosaurid (a group of feathered carnivorous theropods) dinosaur

facts.statement: Researchers in 1993 estimated that the premaxilla of Utahraptor was approximately 250% larger than that of Deinonychus.
facts.quote: According to Kirkland and colleagues in 1993, the premaxilla of U. ostrommaysi was incredibly large compared to that of other dromaeosaurids, perhaps 250% larger than that of Deinonychus.

facts.statement: The tooth row of the Utahraptor premaxilla measured approximately 75 mm in length.
facts.quote: The alveolar process or tooth row of the premaxilla was around 75 mm in length.

facts.statement: The front teeth of the Utahraptor lower jaw were procumbent, meaning they visibly protruded forward.
facts.quote: The teeth of Utahraptor lower jaw were fairly procumbent anteriorly, meaning those towards the front would have visibly protruded forwards.

facts.statement: The second toe claw of the Utahraptor holotype measured 22 cm along its curve and is estimated to be 24 cm in total length.
facts.quote: The second pedal ungual, the bone on the second toe which would have supported this claw, is preserved in the holotype with a 22 cm length when measured along its outside curve, and is estimated to have measured 24 cm in total.

facts.statement: The size of the flexor tubercles on Utahraptor's foot digits suggests it had a stronger grip relative to its body size than Deinonychus.
facts.quote: The size of the flexor tubercles on U. ostrommaysi pedal digits, to which digital flexors would have attached in life, suggests that it had a strong grip, perhaps more so than Deinonychus (which had smaller flexor tubercles) in proportion to body size.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that Utahraptor used its hand claws to slash at prey due to their blade-like construction.
facts.quote: However, they were more laterally compressed and were noted to have been more blade-like in construction, leading Kirkland and colleagues to suggest that U. ostrommaysi might have used them to slash at prey.

facts.statement: Utahraptor was likely slower than Deinonychus and Velociraptor but faster than sauropods, moving at a speed similar to contemporary iguanodonts.
facts.quote: Kirkland and colleagues noted that given the large size of Utahraptor, it was not as fast as Deinonychus and Velociraptor; instead, it would have had a similar speed to the contemporary iguanodonts, though would have been faster than sauropods.

facts.statement: Unlike lighter dromaeosaurids that used hands for balance while kicking, the heavy Utahraptor could likely kick without losing balance and use its hands to kill prey.
facts.quote: It was also suggested that lighter dromaeosaurids such as Velociraptor and Deinonychus relied on their hand claws to handle prey and retain balance while kicking it; in contrast to this, the heavily built Utahraptor may have been able to deliver kicks without the risk of losing balance, freeing the hands and using them to dispatch prey.

facts.statement: Utahraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of theropod dinosaurs commonly called raptors.
facts.quote: Utahraptor is a member of the family Dromaeosauridae, a clade of theropod dinosaurs commonly known as the "raptors".

facts.statement: Utahraptor is considered one of the largest, if not the largest known, members of the Dromaeosauridae family.
facts.quote: Utahraptor is one of the largest, if not the largest-known representative of the family.

facts.statement: James Kirkland and colleagues originally classified Utahraptor in the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae, which is now part of the clade Eudromaeosauria.
facts.quote: In their initial description of the genus, James Kirkland and colleagues placed Utahraptor within the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae, now part of the clade Eudromaeosauria.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis suggested Utahraptor might belong to a clade outside Dromaeosaurinae, though it could be reclassified into Dromaeosaurinae or Velociraptorinae with minor changes.
facts.quote: An analysis in 2019 by Mickey Mortimer and colleagues recovered Achillobator, Deinonychus, Utahraptor and Yixiansaurus in a clade potentially outside of Dromaeosaurinae, though noted that it could be moved to either Dromaeosaurinae or Velociraptorinae in only two steps.

facts.statement: In 2001, researchers led by Kirkland excavated a nine-ton sandstone block in eastern Utah containing Utahraptor fossils.
facts.quote: In 2001, Kirkland and colleagues pursued a graduate student's discovery of a bone protruding from a nine-ton fossil block of sandstone in eastern Utah.

facts.statement: The fossil block contained remains of at least seven Utahraptor individuals, including an adult approximately 4.8 meters long, four juveniles, and a hatchling about 1 meter long.
facts.quote: It was determined to contain the bones of at least seven individuals, including an adult measuring about 4.8 m, four juveniles and a hatchling about 1 m long.

facts.statement: Kirkland hypothesized that the Utahraptor pack became trapped in quicksand while trying to scavenge carrion or attack a mired herbivore.
facts.quote: Kirkland speculated that the Utahraptor pack attempted to scavenge carrion or attack helpless prey mired in quicksand, and were themselves mired in the attempt to feed on the herbivore.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether all Utahraptor individuals in the fossil block became trapped simultaneously or were drawn in one by one.
facts.quote: Whether all the Utahraptor individuals were mired simultaneously or were drawn in, one-by-one is unclear.

facts.statement: Further examination suggests the number of Utahraptor remains in the block may be twice the previously assumed count.
facts.quote: Further examination of the block suggests that the number of Utahraptor remains may be double the amount previously assumed.

facts.statement: The discovery of Utahraptor in a mud trap implies the species exhibited gregarious behavior and possibly post-nestling care.
facts.quote: Additionally, the discovery of Utahraptor in the mud-trap implies it exhibited a degree of post-nestling care and gregariousness.

facts.statement: Utahraptor was a major carnivore in the Early Cretaceous Arches region capable of attacking prey larger than itself.
facts.quote: According to the authors of its description, Utahraptor had an important ecological role as a major carnivore of the paleofauna of the present-day Arches region during the Early Cretaceous, and could probably attack prey larger than itself.

facts.statement: If proven, group hunting by Utahraptors measuring at least 3.5 meters and weighing 70 kg could have killed prey up to 8 meters long and weighing 1 to 2 tons.
facts.quote: Group hunting of individuals of at least 3.5 m and 70 kg, if proven, could have killed 8 m prey of a weight of 1 to 2 t.

facts.statement: Sauropods approximately 20 meters long may have been an important part of the Utahraptor diet.
facts.quote: Additionally, sauropods ranging around 20 m may have been an important part of its diet.

facts.statement: In 2019, Joeckel and colleagues concluded the Yellow Cat Member is older than previously estimated.
facts.quote: Joeckel and colleagues (2019) concluded that the Yellow Cat Member is indeed older than previous estimations.

facts.statement: The Yellow Cat Member was deposited between 139 ± 1.3 million and 134.6 ± 1.7 million years ago, corresponding to the Berriasian to Late Valanginian stages.
facts.quote: The deposition occurred between 139 ± 1.3 million to 134.6 ± 1.7 million years ago, or, Berriasian to Late Valanginian stages.

facts.statement: Utahraptor fossils are currently known only from the upper Yellow Cat Member.
facts.quote: Utahraptor fossils are only currently known within the upper Yellow Cat Member.

facts.statement: During the Berriasian to Late Valanginian, the Yellow Cat Member was a semiarid environment featuring floodplain prairies, riverine forests, and open woodlands dominated by conifers, ferns, and hornworts.
facts.quote: Utahraptor was unearthed from the Yellow Cat Member, which during the Berriasian to Late Valanginian was a semiarid area with floodplain prairies, riverine forests and open woodlands predominated by conifers (Pinophyta), ferns (Polypodiopsida), hornworts (Anthocerotophyta) and other vascular plants.

facts.statement: Charred spores and carbonized plant debris indicate that ancient wildfires occurred during periods of low precipitation in the Utahraptor habitat.
facts.quote: This is supported by the presence of charred spores and other carbonized plant debris in the pollen maceral that indicate the occurrence of ancient wildfires ignited during periods of low precipitation.

facts.statement: In areas where Utahraptor and allosauroids cohabited, the allosauroid was likely dominant, with a relationship analogous to modern bears and wolves.
facts.quote: In areas where they cohabited, the allosauroid was likely dominant, with their relationship possibly being analogous to bears and wolves in modern ecosystems.

facts.statement: In 2018, a 10-year-old student named Kenyon Roberts successfully proposed Utahraptor as the Utah state dinosaur, a proposal approved by the Senate.
facts.quote: In 2018, it was proposed by a 10-year-old elementary school student, Kenyon Roberts, that Utahraptor be the Utah state dinosaur, an act that was approved by the Senate.

facts.statement: On May 23, 2025, the Visitor Center of Utahraptor State Park opened to the public, displaying a Utahraptor skeleton alongside other Dalton Wells dinosaur species.
facts.quote: On May 23, 2025, the Visitor Center of Utahraptor State Park was officially opened to the public, displaying the skeleton of a Utahraptor alongside other Dalton Wells dinosaur species.

facts.statement: Utahraptor is a theropod dinosaur and the only genus in the Utahraptor genus.
facts.quote: Utahraptor ostrommaysi es una especie de dinosaurio terópodo dromeosáurido y único representante del género Utahraptor

facts.statement: Utahraptor lived between 139 and 134 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico Inferior, entre 139 a 134 millones de años, durante el Barremiano y Valanginiano, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Utahraptor is known for being the largest member of the dromaeosaurid family.
facts.quote: Se le conoce sobre todo por ser el mayor representante de la familia de los dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: The holotype of Utahraptor is fragmentary, consisting only of skull parts, a tibia, claws, and some tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Utahraptor es fragmentario pues de él solo se conservan restos del cráneo, una tibia, garras y algunas vértebras caudales

facts.statement: A preserved claw specimen measures 22 cm in length, with estimates suggesting a restored length of over 24 cm.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar de garra posee una longitud preservada de 22 cm y se cree que mediría algo más de 24 cm restaurada

facts.statement: The largest described Utahraptor specimen, BYUVP 15465, is estimated to have reached 7 meters in length and nearly 500 kilograms in weight, comparable to a polar bear.
facts.quote: Se estima que el espécimen de U. ostrommaysi más grande descrito, BYUVP 15465, referido por Erickson et al. 2009 alcanzó hasta 7 metros de largo y algo menos de 500 kilogranos de peso, comparable a un oso polar

facts.statement: In 2012, paleontologist Thomas R. Holtz Jr. proposed that Utahraptor's weight could be comparable to that of a brown bear.
facts.quote: En 2012, el paleontólogo Thomas R. Holtz Jr. propuso que su peso podría ser comparable al de un oso pardo

facts.statement: A 2001 discovery by Kirkland suggests that Utahraptor may be much heavier than previously estimated.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el descubrimiento de Kirkland de 2001 indica que la especie puede ser mucho más pesada de lo estimado previamente

facts.statement: A 2016 measurement by Gregory S. Paul estimated Utahraptor at up to 5.5 meters long and weighing up to 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: La medición de 2016 realizada por Gregory S. Paul estuvo cerca de esta nueva estimación, midiendo hasta 5,5 metros de largo y pesando hasta 300 kilogramos

facts.statement: Like other dromaeosaurids, Utahraptor had large curved claws on its second toe.
facts.quote: Como otros dromeosáuridos, Utahraptor tenía grandes garras curvadas en su segundo dedo del pie

facts.statement: According to Kirkland et al. in 1993, Utahraptor is distinguished by hand claws that are more specialized as cutting blades than in other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Según Kirkland et al. en 1993, Utahraptor puede ser reconocido por las siguientes autapomorfias, garras en la mano que están más especializadas como cuchillas cortantes que en otros dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: In a 2012 revised diagnosis by Turner et al., Utahraptor is distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by an elongated nasal process of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: En el diagnóstico revisado realizado por Turner et al. en 2012, Utahraptor se diferencia de otros dromeosáuridos en, un proceso nasal alargado del premaxilar

facts.statement: The first Utahraptor specimens were found in 1975 by Jim Jensen at the Dalton Wells quarry in central-eastern Utah, near the town of Moab.
facts.quote: Los primeros especímenes de Utahraptor fueron hallados en 1975 por Jim Jensen en la cantera Dalton Wells en la zona centro-este de Utah, cerca del pueblo de Moab

facts.statement: After Carl Limoni found a huge foot claw in October 1991, James Kirkland, Robert Gaston, and Donald Burge discovered additional Utahraptor remains in 1991 at the Gaston Quarry in Grand County, Utah.
facts.quote: Después del hallazgo de una enorme garra del pie por Carl Limoni en octubre de 1991 James Kirkland, Robert Gaston y Donald Burge descubrieron restos adicionales de Utahraptor en 1991 en la cantera Gaston Quarry en Grand County, Utah

facts.statement: These remains were found within the Yellow Cat and Poison Strip Members of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: dentro de los Miembros Yellow Cat y Poison Strip de la Formación Cedar Mountain

facts.statement: Radiometric dating shows that parts of the Cedar Mountain Formation were deposited about 124 million years ago.
facts.quote: Dataciones radiométricas han mostrado que estas partes de la formación Cedar Mountain fueron depositadas hace cerca de 124 millones de años

facts.statement: The Utahraptor holotype, CEUM 184v.86, consists of a second pedal ungual, potentially assigned elements from other specimens, a foot ungual CEUM 184v.294, a tibia CEUM 184v.260, and a premaxilla CEUM 184v.400.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Utahraptor, CEUM 184v.86 consta de un segundo ungual pedal, con elementos potencialmente asignados de otros especímenes, un ungueal del pie, CEUM 184v.294, una tibia, CEUM 184v.260 y premaxilar, CEUM 184v.400

facts.statement: The holotype is housed in the paleontology collections of the Utah State University Eastern Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: El holotipo se encuentra en las colecciones de paleontología del Museo Prehistórico de la Universidad Estatal de Utah Eastern

facts.statement: Brigham Young University, the repository for Jensen's finds, currently holds the largest collection of Utahraptor fossils.
facts.quote: La Universidad Brigham Young, el depósito de los hallazgos de Jensen, actualmente alberga la mayor colección de fósiles de Utahraptor

facts.statement: Although no feathers have been found associated with Utahraptor specimens, strong phylogenetic evidence suggests all dromaeosaurids possessed them.
facts.quote: Aunque nunca se han encontrado plumas en asociación con los ejemplares de Utahraptor, existe fuerte evidencia filogenética que sugiere que todos los dromeosáuridos las poseían

facts.statement: The genus Microraptor is among the oldest dromaeosaurids and is phylogenetically more primitive than Utahraptor.
facts.quote: El género Microraptor está entre los dromeosáuridos más antiguos, y es filogenéticamente más primitivo que Utahraptor

facts.statement: It is debated whether feathers were lost in larger, more advanced dromaeosaurid species, as no evidence currently suggests this occurred.
facts.quote: Hasta el momento, no hay nada que sugiera que las plumas se perdieron en las especies más grandes y avanzadas de dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: In a 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, two Utahraptor foot bones were examined for stress fractures, but none were found.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2001 llevado a cabo por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, 2 huesos del pie referidos a Utahraptor fueron examinados para buscar signos de fracturas de estrés, pero no se halló ninguna

facts.statement: The species Utahraptor ostrommaysorum was named by Kirkland, Gaston, and Burge in 1993.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y la única conocida de Utahraptor hasta el momento, Utahraptor ostrommaysorum, fue nombrada por Kirkland, Gaston y Burge en 1993

facts.statement: The specific name was modified to the plural genitive U. ostrommaysorum by George Olshevsky in 2000.
facts.quote: En 2000, el nombre específico fue modificado por George Olshevsky al genitivo plural U. ostrommaysorum.

facts.statement: In 2019, Costa and David criticized the use of the species name U. ostrommaysorum because it lacks a clear justification or explanation.
facts.quote: Thiago Vernaschi V. Costa y Normand David en 2019 criticaron el uso del nombre de la especie U. ostrommaysorum ya que no tiene una justificación o explicación clara.

facts.statement: Utahraptor is a member of the family Dromaeosauridae, a clade of theropod dinosaurs commonly known as "raptors".
facts.quote: Utahraptor es un miembro de la familia Dromaeosauridae, un clado de dinosaurios terópodos comúnmente conocidos como "raptores".

facts.statement: Utahraptor is the largest genus in the family and belongs to the same dinosaur clade as Velociraptor, Deinonychus, and Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Utahraptor es el género más grande de la familia, y pertenece al mismo clado de dinosaurios como Velociraptor, Deinonychus o Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: It is classified in the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae, which is found in the clade Eudromaeosauria.
facts.quote: Se clasifica en la subfamilia Dromaeosaurinae, que se encuentra en el clado Eudromaeosauria.

facts.statement: Utahraptor lived during the Valanginian stage, from 137.05 to 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers noted that due to its enormous size, Utahraptor was not as fast as Deinonychus and Velociraptor but would have had a speed similar to contemporary iguanodontians and faster than sauropods.
facts.quote: Kirkland et al. señaló que dado el enorme tamaño de Utahraptor, no era tan rápido como Deinonychus y Velociraptor, sino que habría tenido una velocidad similar a la de los iguanodontianos contemporáneos y siendo más rápido que los saurópodos.

facts.statement: The thickness of the tibia indicates that the animal had significant leg strength for killing prey.
facts.quote: Además, el grosor de la tibia indica que el animal tenía una fuerza de pierna significativa para matar presas.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul suggested that Utahraptor was not particularly fast and would have been an ambush predator feeding on large dinosaurs like contemporary iguanodontians and therizinosaurians.
facts.quote: Según el paleontólogo Gregory S. Paul, Utahraptor no era particularmente rápido y habría sido un cazador de emboscadas que se alimentaba de grandes dinosaurios como los iguanodontianos y terizinosaurianos contemporáneos con los que compartía su entorno.

facts.statement: Like other dromaeosaurines, it is possible that Utahraptor relied heavily on its jaws to dispatch prey, more so than other types of dromaeosaurs, such as velociraptorines.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros dromeosaurinos, es posible que también dependiera en gran medida de sus mandíbulas para despachar presas, más que otros tipos de dromeosáuridos, como los velociraptorinos.

facts.statement: In 2001, researchers discovered a fossil block weighing 9 tons in eastern Utah containing the bones of at least seven Utahraptor individuals.
facts.quote: En 2001, Kirkland et al, persiguieron el descubrimiento de un estudiante graduado de un hueso que sobresalía de un bloque fósil de piedra arenisca de 9 toneladas en el este de Utah.

facts.statement: The fossil block contained bones of at least seven individuals, including an adult measuring about 4.8 meters, four juveniles, and a hatchling approximately 1 meter long.
facts.quote: Se determinó que contenía los huesos de al menos siete individuos, incluido un adulto que medía unos 4,8 metros, cuatro juveniles y una cría de aproximadamente 1 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Kirkland speculated that the Utahraptor pack tried to scavenge or attack defenseless prey stuck in quicksand, and they themselves became trapped while attacking the herbivore.
facts.quote: Kirkland especuló que la manada de Utahraptor intentó hurgar en la carroña o atacar a presas indefensas atascadas en arenas movedizas, y ellos mismos estaban empantanados en el intento de atacar al herbívoro.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether all Utahraptor individuals were trapped simultaneously or attracted one by one.
facts.quote: No está claro si todos los individuos de Utahraptor quedaron atrapados simultáneamente o fueron atraídos, uno por uno.

facts.statement: Sculptor Raymond Persinger was included in the original summary by James Kirkland, referencing Persinger's concepts regarding the claw structure.
facts.quote: El escultor Raymond Persinger fue incluido en el resumen original de James Kirkland referenciando los conceptos de Persinger acerca de la estructura de la garra.
